memory_update.text: RMGNF/RHI Magnesita N.V. is the best direct U.S.-accessible reference asset for Indian refractory consolidation, but exposure must be traced through RHI Magnesita India and related-party dynamics.
MTX/Minerals Technologies is the most relevant primary U.S.-exchange underfollowed candidate found so far; key gap is proving India-specific refractory systems exposure.

MCRUF/Morgan Advanced Materials is a speculative OTC shadow candidate because its thermal-products portfolio overlaps high-temperature industrial processes, but India steel/cement linkage is unverified.
Tata Steel capacity expansion is useful as a customer-demand anchor for refractory suppliers; use plant-level procurement/tender searches to identify embedded refractory vendors.
The U.S.-listed universe for Indian refractory consolidation is sparse; later layers should include India-listed names and private/unlisted suppliers if mandate permits non-U.S. assets.

node: Indian refractories embedded in steel and cement capacity expansion
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around Indian refractory consolidation with a two-lane funnel. The strongest direct reference asset is RHI Magnesita via its Indian listed subsidiary, but it is not a primary U.S. exchange listing; U.S. access appears to be OTC. The underfollowed U.S.-accessible lane is thin but includes Minerals Technologies as a direct NYSE-listed refractory systems supplier to steel and industrial markets, plus OTC-traded specialty ceramics/materials names with plausible exposure. Tata Steel is included only as a demand-anchor/customer context candidate because its Indian capacity expansion helps validate the downstream refractory demand driver, not because it is the chokepoint beneficiary.
